grid_audit_NEW.summary: None of the three grids is complete under the rule: 4-9 bare n/a cells each, and v1a has 7 empty cells. Most n/a reasons that are given are sound (read only, single call, model has no effects). The clearly wrong one is v1a 'writes x malformed: we send it'. About half of cited cells (43/81, 53%) have a matching acceptance test; credential-expiry, rate-limit and dependency-outage cells are the ones most often cited but untested. The grid adds about 400-500 words, and the failure section is about 2.6x the OLD size (mean 794 vs 311 words). Total docs grew about 8% (mean 10,278 vs 9,479 words).

grid_made_worse: Length: the failure section is about 2.6x longer (311 to 794 words); total docs +8%. The cross-cutting scenario table survives alongside the grid, so outcomes like 'uncertain' and 'partial move' are stated twice.

Untested citations: about half the grid cells cite a ticket that has no matching acceptance item. They look like tested coverage but are only claims (credential expiry, rate limits, DB or JWKS outage).
Wrong or bare n/a: v1a 'writes x malformed: n/a we send it'; v1a 'Vertex x duplicate' and 'Postgres x rate limited' as bare n/a; 18 bare n/a across the three runs, against the rule.

Displacement: OLD-style items dropped in NEW runs. v1a lost proposal expiry and the call-cap test, and v1c named no customer-text injection case. In all three NEW runs cancel-all appears only as injected staff text, not as a customer's own 'cancel all my appointments' request (all three OLD runs tested it directly). Model retirement appears as a row in only one NEW run.

No effect on scope variance: v1b still cut move/cancel to phase 2 and swapped login for reference+phone, so its partial-move cell became an open decision. The grid stabilises the infrastructure-failure rows but not the product-level choices that drive the rest of the variance.
verdict: The grid raised coverage by about 10 situations per run (25.3 to 35.3) and moved the shared core from 20 to 30. All of the gain is integration-level failures (rate limits, credential expiry, DB, JWKS, model quota, malformed payloads) that no OLD run had. Run-to-run similarity rose slightly (mean Jaccard 0.77 to 0.81), but 11 of 41 situations are still in only one or two NEW runs. Known-gap coverage rose modestly (7.0 to 7.7 of 9) and is not consistent: partial-move, call-cap test, pass bar and reconciliation drill are each still missing or partial in at least one NEW run. Only v1c closed all nine. Recommend keeping the grid, but require each cited cell to point to an acceptance line, forbid bare n/a, and add product-level rows (customer cancel-all, proposal expiry, call cap, pass bar, reconciliation drill) as a fixed checklist rather than leaving them to the per-integration grid.
